title: Unit 2.4 Boolean logic — review and test
specPoints: Covers all of 2.4: AND/OR/NOT gates and symbols, truth tables with intermediate columns, logic diagrams from and to expressions, scenarios
Teachers: switch on Teacher view for the mark scheme. The A-level extension is **not** examined and is not in this test.
learn: Complete any 2- or 3-input truth table accurately
Draw and read logic diagrams with up to three gates
Turn a worded scenario into an expression and a circuit
hook: Three rules: count rows in binary, one column per gate, brackets first. That is the whole unit.

list: AND: both. OR: at least one. NOT: flip (draw the bubble).
n inputs → 2ⁿ rows, counted in binary.
Intermediate column for every gate; inner brackets first.
Expression → diagram: inner gate nearest the inputs. Diagram → expression: label every output.

try.title: Scratch space (allowed only if your teacher says so)
p: Checking a table by code is fine practice but not available in the real exam.

exam.q: Draw the symbols for an AND gate and a NOT gate.
model: AND: flat-backed D-shape, two inputs, one output (1). NOT: triangle with inversion bubble, one input, one output (1).

exam.q: Complete the truth table for `Q = NOT A OR B`.
Complete the truth table for `Q = (A OR B) AND NOT C` for all eight combinations.
Draw a logic diagram for `Q = A AND (B OR NOT C)`.
model: NOT on C (1). OR with B and NOT C (1). AND with A and the OR output, labelled Q (1).

exam.q: Write the expression for the circuit: A feeds a NOT gate; the NOT output and B feed an AND gate; the AND output and C feed an OR gate whose output is Q.
model: Q = (NOT A AND B) OR C (2).

exam.q: A heating system turns on (H = 1) when the thermostat calls for heat (T = 1) AND the timer is active (M = 1), OR when the boost button (B = 1) is pressed. Write the expression and state the output for T = 0, M = 1, B = 1.
model: H = (T AND M) OR B (1 structure, 1 brackets/operators correct). For T=0, M=1, B=1: H = 1 (1).

exam.q: Explain why a truth table for three inputs must have eight rows.
model: Each input can be 0 or 1 (1), so the number of combinations is 2 × 2 × 2 = 2³ = 8 (1).

exam.q: Give **one** reason why intermediate columns are useful when completing a truth table for an expression with more than one gate.
model: They break the problem into one gate at a time so each column depends only on earlier ones (1), reducing errors and showing working that can earn marks even if the final column is wrong (1).

teacher.timing: 40 min: review 3 · test 30 · self-mark 7. 20 marks. Bands: 16+ secure; 11–15 developing; below 11 reteach truth tables with physical switches.
misconceptions: Most lost marks: missing bubble on NOT, missing rows, missing brackets. Three mechanical habits fix all three.
say: 'Binary rows. One column per gate. Brackets first.'
teacher.skip: For 20 minutes drop Q7 and Q8 (4 marks), mark out of 16.
differentiation: Support: provide the input columns pre-filled for Q2 and Q3.
Stretch (not for marks): simplify Q4's expression if C is always 0.
